name: Isotonic distributional regression (IDR)
title: The whole payout distribution, under one order rule
what: Predict a full distribution, not one number, assuming only “worse stress never means a bigger payout distribution.”
pick_line: Learn one monotone stress index from several covariates, then fit IDR on that score.
data: Public filings (Fed DFAST results, FR Y-9C, SCB PDFs); descriptive only
one: Stress pre-tax income gives 15% skill on next payouts; the SCB itself has none.

left.sub: skill vs climatology on raw payout/RWA (worse than no model)

findings.h: Projected pre-tax income describes payout ranks four times better than drawdown.
findings.t: Leave-one-year-out CRPS skill over climatology: 15.0% for pre-tax income vs 3.9% for drawdown (both p = 0.003, the floor with 299 shuffles).

findings.h: The buffer itself (SCB) says nothing about payouts.
findings.t: 2021–2025: SCB skill −1.9% (p = 0.24) though it tracks drawdown closely (Spearman 0.92); drawdown 7.0%, pre-tax income 11.3%. 37.9% of firm-years sit at the 2.5% floor.
findings.note: Bar for SCB drawn at zero; its skill is negative (−1.9%).

findings.h: The relationship weakened after 2020 except for the worst decile.
findings.t: A 2013–19 fit still beats 2021–25 climatology (7.0%), but not the reverse (−6.1%). Ranking persistence fell: Kendall τ 0.82–0.84 (2014–16) to 0.40–0.69 (2021–25).

chart.title: Fit on one era, scored on the other
